steps.text:
Materials Needed: NEW Units: OLL, OLD, OLT, OST, ILD, IND. Letter Tiles: A-Z plus F, L, S, Z, CH, TH, CK, SH, WH, TCH. Units: ALL, ANG, ING, ONG, UNG, ANK, INK, ONK, UNK.

Overview: Students learn the last set of Units for quite a while. In each of these Units, the vowel makes its Long sound (says its own name). Introduce the 4 units that start with O, then the 2 that start with I. Point out that most of them have an L after the vowel. Mark Unit syllables by drawing a box around all 3 letters.
Repeat this nonsense word, then make just its FIRST sound. Ready? HENCH.
Expected: Hench, /h/
Point to the tile that makes that sound.
Student points to the H tile.
Now I want the LAST sound. CRENT.
Expected: Crent, /t/
Point to that tile.
Student points to T.
Now for the MIDDLE sound. Say both the sound AND its keyword. Ready? SNISH.
Expected: Snish, /i/-Itchy.
Repeat First Sound for: FLISHT, THRAP, BRONT. Last Sound for: DRIMP, BRUZZ, PLOTH, GLAV. Vowel Sound for: GLOCK, DRANT, RUCK, SMETCH.

sections.title: D: NEW TEACHING #1: Units Starting with O

steps.text: What does this say? Is it a Digraph or a Unit?
Expected: ALL. Unit.
Today, you're going to be learning 6 more Units.
If A-L-L says ALL, what do you think O-L-L will say? Let me make a word out of it.
That's something you might eat with dinner. What's that word?
Expected: Roll.
So what does O-L-L say? In /oll/, is the vowel making its Short sound? No. It is saying its own name... O. That's why it is a Unit.
Here's another Unit. This one can be a word all by itself. What does it say?
Expected: Old.
What sound is that vowel making? Its own name. Although it LOOKS like a Closed syllable, the vowel is NOT making its Short sound.
Build SOLD, SCOLD. Note why we use C and not K (O is not a Watch Out vowel).
In this Unit, the O says its Own Name. So what does this unit say?
Expected: OLT.
Build COLT, JOLT, BOLT.
This is the tricky Unit. As a Unit, the O says its own name, so it says OST. But in 3 words, O-S-T acts like a regular Closed syllable and says /ost/ (short o). Those words are LOST, COST, and FROST.
Build MOST, POST to show it acting as a Unit.

sections.title: E: NEW TEACHING #2: Units Starting with I

steps.text: Here's a Unit that does NOT start with O. Since it's a Unit, do you think the vowel will make its Short sound or say its Own Name?
Expected: Its own name.
Right. So this Unit says ILD. What does it say?
Expected: Ild.
Build CHILD, WILD.
What do you think this one says?
Expected: Ind.
Build MIND, RIND, GRIND. Then build WIND.
I need to warn you about 1 word. WIND. That's one way to say it. What's the other way?
Expected: Wind (long I).
Right. It can either say Wind (wind your watch) or Wind (the wind is blowing). You won't know which way to say it unless you see it in a sentence.

sections.title: F: Spell Real Words with Fingers, then Tiles

steps.text: Now you're going to finger spell. The first word is MOLD. Repeat that word.
Expected: MOLD
Use your fingers to break it into sounds. But raise only ONE finger for the OLD sound, because you bring down only one tile.
Student raises thumb for /m/, index for /old/.
Double check by blending those sounds. Now change one tile to make that word say MILD.
Student swaps OLD for ILD.
Dictate the remaining words: FOLD, GOLD, JOLT, VOLT, COLT, COLD, TOLD, TROLL, SCROLL, BLIND, BIND, HOST, HIND.

sections.title: I: Read Words Through Word Frame

steps.text: Now you're going to read words through the word frame. If you know the word for sure, just say it. Otherwise, sound it out.
Let's read some phrases. Tell me the WHO, DID WHAT, WHERE, and ADD-ON phrases.
Now find every word that ends in a Unit, and box off the Unit on the screen.
Now you'll read some sentences. Read the first sentence to yourself, then read it out loud.

payload: A blind man couldn't find us at the mall but didn't mind.
The cold duck wouldn't hold still in the old shack with frost on it.
The small child didn't step on the hind leg of the wild frog.
One kind host won't tell Hank to sit on a bench and shut up.
She'll hold on to the strong dog when she goes on a stroll.
He'll scold the wild child in class, but he won't tell on him.
The bold colt is sick and won't kick in the spring.
If it weren't for Mom, you'd bring a crust with mold on it.

steps.text: Mark the WHO phrase, DID WHAT phrase, WHERE phrase, and ADD-ON phrase.
Student marks phrases and reads sentence with phrasing (pausing between chunks).
Now you're ready to read a story. Preread the story and figure out the tough words. Then read it out loud to me.

payload.title: The Colt
payload.text: Dad and Pam went to find the colt. It was a cold stroll, but the child didn't mind. Dad led her with his hand. Pam was blind. Dad would put Pam on the back of the colt. It was a thrill to hug his neck as she sat on his back. When the colt went on a trot, Pam felt the jolt of his strong legs. 'Thank you, Dad,' she said when she had to stop.

steps.text: Have the student retell the story in their own words to check comprehension. Alternative stories in manual: 'Tim Wasn't Kind', 'The Skunk', 'The Wild Colt'.
